title: Causal Scrubbing as an Empirical Test of Formal Mechanistic Explanations

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Tests whether the effort of formalization improves causal accuracy of mechanistic explanations. If more formal explanations yield better scrubbing results, this justifies the investment in formalization. Directly actionable for the mech interp community.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Causal scrubbing requires understanding and implementing activation patching at a detailed level. Constructing two levels of mechanistic explanation (intuitive vs. formal) for the same model requires deep mech interp expertise. This is advanced research, not beginner-accessible.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Two explanation levels for one model on one task, with causal scrubbing evaluation. The scope is moderate if the model and task are already well-understood, but constructing the formal explanation from scratch could be time-consuming.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Novelty not assessed due to partial Wave 3 completion.
